 Food pantry demand grows as SNAP benefits decline in Michigan 
 By Brayden Willis Published : Oct. 18, 2026 at 7:22 PM EDT | Updated : 11 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google JACKSON, Mich. (News 10) - Food pantries in Michigan say demand is rising and shelves are emptying faster as changes to SNAP benefits take effect across the state.
 New data from the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services shows more than 172,000 Michiganders have lost food assistance benefits since last June. Nearly 57,000 of them are children. Overall, SNAP enrollment is down more than 12%.
 Pantry sees rising demand
 Brenda Hughes is the founder of Jackson Michigan Giving Back to the Community, a nonprofit that has distributed food, clothing and basic necessities since 1991.
 “The demand for food skyrocketing at this time... like, we can’t keep up with it at this point. We truly can’t keep up with it,” Hughes said.
 Hughes said she has noticed new faces visiting the pantry.
 “People that you never thought you would see come into a food bank... From last year, I see from people that work at the hospital, bus drivers coming in here... People assume that the cars that people drive, assume that these people don’t need help. They need help,” Hughes said.
 Line wraps around the street
 Dave Chamberlain, a five-year volunteer at the pantry, said the line Sunday morning wrapped around the street.
 “It doesn’t matter if it’s a sunny day, rainy day, snowy day... they’re always hungry,” Chamberlain said.
 One woman in line, who did not want to be identified, told News 10 she works more than one job to put food on the table but would have to quit one of them to qualify for SNAP.
 Hughes said people should not make assumptions about pantry visitors.
 “Never judge a book by its cover. First, read the book and then get to know the book before you judge anyone that comes into a food pantry, because everybody wasn’t born with a silver spoon,” Hughes said.
 Nearly 300 households served
 Volunteers said they served nearly 300 individual households Sunday, ranging from one to as many as seven people each.
 More information is available on the organization’s website: https://jacksonmichigangivingback.org/
